business_rule: The session is marked as permanent if the '_permanent' key is set to true.
The session is considered modified if any changes are made to the session data.
If the session is empty and modified, the corresponding cookie will be deleted.
A cookie will be set if the session has been modified or if the session is permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is true.
The expiration time for a permanent session is set to the current time plus the application's permanent session lifetime.
If the session cannot be opened due to a configuration error, a null session will be created.
The session cookie name is determined by the SESSION_COOKIE_NAME configuration value.
The session cookie domain is determined by the SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN configuration value.
The session cookie path is determined by the SESSION_COOKIE_PATH configuration value or falls back to APPLICATION_ROOT or '/' if not set.
The session cookie is marked as HttpOnly based on the SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY configuration value.
The session cookie is marked as secure based on the SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE configuration value.
The SameSite attribute for the session cookie is determined by the SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE configuration value.
The session cookie can be partitioned based on the SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED configuration value.
The response method requires either positional or keyword arguments, but not both.
If no arguments are provided to the response method, None is serialized.
The dumps method uses a default function to serialize objects that are not natively serializable to JSON.
The ensure_ascii attribute determines whether non-ASCII characters are replaced with escape sequences during JSON serialization.
The sort_keys attribute determines whether the keys in serialized dictionaries are sorted.
The compact attribute controls the formatting of the response output based on the debug mode.
The default value for the compact attribute is None, which means it will not add indentation or newlines unless in debug mode.
If the current application context is available, the dumps function uses the app's json.dumps method to serialize data.
If the current application context is not available, the dumps function uses the default parameter to handle serialization.
If the current application context is available, the dump function uses the app's json.dump method to serialize data and write it to a file.
If the current application context is not available, the dump function uses the default parameter to handle serialization.
If the current application context is available, the loads function uses the app's json.loads method to deserialize data.
If the current application context is not available, the loads function uses the standard json.loads method to deserialize data.
If the current application context is available, the load function uses the app's json.load method to deserialize data from a file.
If the current application context is not available, the load function uses the standard json.load method to deserialize data from a file.
The jsonify function requires an active application context and uses the app's json.response method to serialize arguments as JSON.
In debug mode, the output of the jsonify function is formatted with indentation for easier reading.
